name: Dentrix
tagline: Practice management software for dental offices: scheduling, charting, billing, and insurance claims in one system of record.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Sold through quotes and bundles rather than public per-seat pricing.

verdictSummary: Dentrix is not an app, it is the clinical and financial system of record for a dental practice, and the hard parts are all the parts nobody wants to build. Electronic claims go out through clearinghouses with payer-specific rules, imaging hooks into sensors and pano machines, charting has to match how hygienists actually work, and every byte of it is PHI under HIPAA with audit trails and BAAs attached. An agent can absolutely produce a pretty appointment book and a tooth chart in an afternoon. It cannot produce the claim scrubbing, the eligibility checks, the recall engine, or the legal posture that lets you bill insurance and survive an audit. And if the practice already runs on it, there are years of ledgers, perio histories, and imaging references inside that nobody is migrating by hand.
coreLoopDIY: A local-only appointment book plus per-patient treatment notes and a clickable tooth chart, with no billing, no claims, and no real patient data.
requirements: Local machine or small VPS you control
Honest acceptance that this is a toy and not a PHI system
whatYouLose: Electronic insurance claims, attachments, and real-time eligibility through a clearinghouse
Imaging integration: sensors, pano, intraoral cameras, and the bridges to third-party imaging software
HIPAA posture: audit logging, access controls, backups, BAAs, breach liability someone else carries
Recall and reactivation engines, treatment plan tracking, and the financial ledger your accountant expects
Support that a front desk can call at 8am when the schedule will not open
moatNotes: Claims clearinghouses and imaging hardware bridges are the real lock, and the patient ledger history is the chain.
whyPeopleStillPay: A dental practice is a small business that bills insurers, stores legally protected health records, and loses real money every hour the front desk cannot see the schedule. Dentrix is paid for because it is the thing that touches the clearinghouse, the imaging sensor, the payment terminal, and the state records retention rule all at once, and because someone else is contractually on the hook when it breaks. A homegrown version shifts all of that liability onto the dentist, who is not a software company and should not become one. The switch cost is also brutal: years of ledgers, perio charts, and imaging pointers that only move cleanly through a paid conversion service.
notes: The tooth chart is a weekend; the claims pipeline and the chain of custody are not. The moat is HIPAA liability plus clearinghouse and imaging integrations, with a decade of patient ledgers holding the door shut.
prompt:
Build a local-only, single-practitioner dental appointment and charting demo. This is a personal tool and a learning exercise, not a HIPAA-compliant system, and it must never be used with real patient data.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js 15 with the App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind
- SQLite via Drizzle ORM, file at ./data/practice.db
- Runs with `npm run dev` on localhost only, no auth, no cloud, no telemetry

In scope:
1. Patients: name, DOB, phone, email, free-text alerts field. Full CRUD, searchable list.
2. Appointment book: day view and week view, 15 minute slots, 8am to 6pm, two chairs. Create, drag to move, resize to change duration, cancel with a reason. Color by status: scheduled, confirmed, seated, complete, no-show.
3. Tooth chart: clickable SVG of 32 adult teeth using universal numbering. Per tooth, record a condition from a short fixed list (sound, caries, restored, crown, missing, implant) and a free-text note. Persist per patient, show the chart state as of today.
4. Treatment notes: append-only notes per patient, timestamped, with the appointment they belong to. Never editable after save, only amendable by adding a new note that references the old one.
5. Recall: flag patients with no completed appointment in the last six months, list them on a dashboard with their phone number. No sending, just the list.
6. Export: a single button that dumps all tables to JSON into ./exports, timestamped.

Explicitly out of scope, do not attempt, do not stub with fake success:
- Insurance claims, eligibility checks, clearinghouse submission, CDT code billing
- Imaging, sensor capture, or any third-party imaging bridge
- Payments, ledgers, statements, or accounts receivable
- Multi-user accounts, role permissions, audit trails, or any HIPAA control
- SMS or email sending of any kind

Seed the database with 12 fake patients and two weeks of fake appointments so the UI is not empty. Put a persistent banner at the top of every page reading: DEMO ONLY, NOT FOR REAL PATIENT DATA. Any config goes in .env, committed as .env.example with no secrets. Write a README that lists the out-of-scope items above verbatim so future-you does not forget what this cannot do.
